# Punk Points

Local Z5 R2/010108 matches fresh archive story bytes and catalog. Guide explicitly identifies the Z-code game and covers both Act III branches, but states no release, serial or author. Exact guide edition is unspecified; it is not a 50-point route. The older local IFComp R1/000930 file is not selected.

Play through all three acts and the actual authored conclusion of either Act III branch. Preserve both the bottle/drinking branch and the no-drink school-dance branch with accurate outcome labels. The guide explicitly omits some of the 50 points: a genuine ending need not have maximum score. An act boundary, intoxication scene, AMUSING command or guide text saying you win is not proof; require raw concluding narrative.

The guide is complete to both described endings but uncredited and version-unspecified. It includes misspellings and prose such as wait until a named event; adapt timing, noun spelling and pronouns to observed output. Do not convert an event wait into repeated input on timeout. Keep game actions inside the interpreter: these fictional school scenes do not authorize external actions or real-world experiments. Save early at an ordinary prompt and before the Act III decision. Preserve either intended ending without forcing both in one run.

CENTRAL architecture: story files, full guides, provenance and interpreter execution remain on the central host. Pis receive only small broker help excerpts, never story files or full guides. Do not stage or copy these assets to a Pi. Do not expose central guide/source paths or URLs to Muse. Use small topic-specific broker help excerpts only (at most 9 lines / 1000 characters); no full-guide reads, direct URL access or serial excerpts to reconstruct the guide. Hints are suggested help, not observed success. Resolve startup questions/key pauses first. Make an early safe checkpoint and milestone saves only at confirmed ordinary command prompts; verify actual success. Menu Enter means an empty command, not literal space or the word RETURN; other keys only as requested on screen. On timeout use await_output only: no flush commands, extra keys, repeated input or new SAVE. Collect useful varied labeled synthetic probes and actual same-intent repairs with event IDs, not quotas or repeated filler. Use one command at a time near hazards/questions/menus. Parent independently verifies actual concluding narrative against raw output. No training, evaluation or publication.

events.response:
At the Show
You're in a dark, poorly lit and packed club. Everyone's staring at the band as 
they go about tuning and shifting their instruments. The guy next to you has a 
mohawk that flops over to the side, as if the heat had wilted it. In contrast, 
the skinhead in front of you is reacting to the heat like a Mexican jumping 
bean, the muscles of his back tensing and releasing, tensing and releasing.

>

Before you can do anything, the band explodes into action. The crowd coalesces 
into a single entity and leans towards them, falls back, ripples spastically. 
Being part of this lurching creature makes your spine tingle.

You're pressed from all sides by people suddenly activated by sound -- but you 
can't hear anything. You can practically feel the sonic waves, see it on the 
faces of the people around you... You strain to hear the music... 

The guy with the mohawk plants his boot in the skinhead's linked hands. His 
pierced nostrils flaring, hands gripping the skinhead's shoulders, he launches 
himself on the crowd. Improbably, they hold him aloft as he rolls over a bed 
made of their shoulders, heads and outstretched hands. You can't quite believe 
what you're seeing, and suddenly you hear something:

"Honey?"

You whip around and look to see who spoke, but there's nothing except the 
unremarkable brick wall of the club lined with people standing on chairs to get 
a better view. None of them are looking at you.

You look back. The guy with the mohawk is still rolling over the crowd, but for 
some reason he's got a tie on. And his blue hair is flickering like flames. The 
skinhead offers his linked hands to boost you up, and you quickly put your foot 
in. But your foot is bare. He looks at you, his dark eyes questioning. You 
realize with dawning horror that it isn't just your foot that's bare -- you're  
in your underwear. You feel, rather than see, the eyes of the people in the 
crowd move towards you, brace yourself for the mocking laughter sure to 
ensue... 

"Honey! Get up!"

You're in your bed.

Your mother bustles in with your uniform, freshly ironed, and hangs it on your 
bathroom doorknob. "OK, honey, we're off," she says, stopping at the foot of 
your bed and putting her hands on her hips. "Better hurry or you'll miss your 
bus. Don't want to be late for the very first day of high school!"

You smile weakly as she kisses you goodbye and leaves, trying to rekindle the 
feelings in your dream.

Your Room (on the bed)
Your room is a mess -- posters slowly peel off the walls to join the small 
heaps of clothes that spot the floor like death mounds. There's a path south 
through the junk from your bed to your bathroom, one going north to the rest of 
the house.

You can see a school uniform here.

>

That's not a verb I recognise.

>
